articles.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
articles.description:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded
Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.
Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.
In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.

Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner
The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations.
Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.

articles.title: Panama submits request to join Expansion of the Information Technology Agreement
articles.description: Panama has submitted a request to join the 2015 Expansion of the Information Technology Agreement (ITA II), the Chair of the Committee of Participants on the Expansion of Trade in Information Technology Products, Mr Shih-Chun Weng of Chinese Taipei, informed members at a meeting on 19 November. Panama said joining ITA II will help it to advance its goal of a more knowledge-based, innovation-driven and technologically advanced economy.

articles.title: Applications open for WIPO-WTO Executive Programme on Intellectual Property Issues
articles.description: The Secretariat of the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) and the Secretariat of the World Trade Organization (WTO) are now accepting applications for the WIPO-WTO Executive Programme on Intellectual Property Issues for Senior Government Officials. The activity will take place from 1 to 12 February 2027 at the headquarters of the WIPO and of the WTO in Geneva, Switzerland.
articles.titleJa: WIPO-WTO知的財産問題に関する幹部プログラムの募集を開始
articles.summary: WIPOとWTOが共同で、政府高官向けの知的財産問題に関する幹部プログラムの参加者を募集しています。

articles.title: Spotlight on trade fundamentals at annual WTO student event
articles.description: Over 200 students joined policymakers, executives and thought leaders on 18 November at the WTO to discuss trade fundamentals at the WTO's annual student-only event on trade, titled WTO 101: Trade Rules!. Now in its third year, the event saw spirited discussions on the key issues facing the multilateral system and its implications for the next generation.
articles.titleJa: WTO年次学生イベントで貿易の基礎に焦点
articles.summary: 200人以上の学生がWTO年次イベントで貿易の基礎と多角的貿易システムの課題について議論しました。

articles.title: Trade Policy Review: Peru
articles.description: The sixth review of the trade policies and practices of Peru takes place on 18 and 20 November 2026. The basis for the review is a report by the WTO Secretariat and a report by the Government of Peru.
articles.titleJa: 貿易政策レビュー：ペルー
articles.summary: ペルーの貿易政策と慣行に関する第6回レビューが2026年11月に実施されます。

articles.title: New trade-restrictive measures surge but WTO members step up trade facilitation efforts
articles.description: The pace of newly-introduced tariffs and other non-facilitating measures rose sharply in the first half of 2026, while the stockpile of such measures reached a record level, according to the WTO Director-General's latest annual overview of developments in the international trading environment. At the same time, WTO members introduced a significant number of trade-facilitating measures, helping to sustain global trade flows despite heightened geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainty.
articles.titleJa: 新たな貿易制限措置が急増するも、WTO加盟国は貿易円滑化努力を強化
articles.summary: 2026年前半に新たな貿易制限措置が急増しましたが、WTO加盟国は貿易円滑化措置を強化しています。

articles.title: DDG Nordquist: Global trade is adapting, not retreating
articles.description: Global trade has demonstrated remarkable resilience despite geopolitical tensions, supply chain disruptions and trade restrictions, with businesses adapting through diversification and new trading partnerships, Deputy Director-General DJ Nordquist said at the 16th Asian Logistics, Maritime and Aviation Conference in Hong Kong, China, on 16 November. Highlighting stronger-than-expected trade growth and the continued importance of WTO rules, she called for more resilient global supply chains, deeper international cooperation and reforms to ensure the multilateral trading system remains fit for today's challenges. The text of her speech is below.
articles.titleJa: ノルドクイスト副事務局長：グローバル貿易は適応しており、後退ではない
articles.summary: ノルドクイストWTO副事務局長は、地政学的緊張下でもグローバル貿易は適応し回復力を見せていると述べました。

articles.title: Goods Council agrees to modernize notification reporting, reviews trade concerns
articles.description: The WTO's Council for Trade in Goods (CTG) adopted a decision to improve annual reporting on notifications and the WTO Notifications Portal. It also reviewed an updated Secretariat report indicating that 35% of the 241 trade concerns raised in the Council between 1995 and May 2026 had been reported as fully or partially resolved. Members considered 38 trade concerns, including five raised for the first time, and discussed several issues relating to tariff renegotiations under Article XXVIII of the GATT.
articles.titleJa: 物品理事会、通報報告の近代化に合意し、貿易上の懸念を審査
articles.summary: WTO物品理事会は通報報告の改善に合意し、解決済みの貿易上の懸念をレビューしました。

articles.title: Ireland contributes EUR 200,000 to strengthen trade opportunities in developing countries
articles.description: Ireland is contributing EUR 200,000 (approximately CHF 185,000) to the Standards and Trade Development Facility (STDF) in 2026 to strengthen sanitary and phytosanitary capacity in developing and least-developed countries. The contribution will support STDF activities that help countries meet international food safety and animal and plant health standards, as well as facilitate safe and inclusive trade.
articles.titleJa: アイルランドが途上国の貿易機会強化に20万ユーロを拠出

articles.title: Members review LDC support, discuss public health and small business IP assistance
articles.description: At a meeting of the Council for Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS) on 12-13 November, members reviewed special provisions for least developed countries (LDCs) and shared experiences on how governments can implement the TRIPS Agreement, achieve public health objectives, and help small businesses benefit from IP protection. The meeting also concluded the review of IP implementing legislation for Samoa, launched a review of Vanuatu's legislation, and received updates on notifications, pandemic preparedness, and other issues.
articles.titleJa: 加盟国、後発開発途上国支援をレビュー、公衆衛生と中小企業IP支援を議論

articles.title: South Africa notifies launch of safeguard investigation into certain non-wired float glass products
articles.description: On 11 November 2026, South Africa notified the WTO’s Committee on Safeguards regarding the initiation on 3 November 2026 of a safeguard investigation into imports of certain non-wired float glass products.
articles.titleJa: 南アフリカ、特定の非線入フロートガラス製品に対するセーフガード調査の開始を通知
